*This is a continuation of my previous writing about using agentic skills for personal workflow automation.*  
[*Article 1*](https://nilanka-weeraman.github.io/configuring_using_agent_skills/) *explains how to setup skills & use with Codex*  
[*Article 2*](https://nilanka-weeraman.github.io/using_codex_background/) *explains how to run codex as a background agent for a streamlit frontend.*

As of now, I have a working app running on my PC using Codex as a background agent, which does a pretty good job \!. My next goals were to (1) convert the codex based agent to a langchain or langgraph and (2) deploy this to the cloud \- so I could run my workflow from anywhere. 

For this endeavor I wanted to choose Antigravity as my coding agent. Main reason being that I wanted to try out the recently launched [gemini 3.1 capabilities](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-3-1-pro/).

On a separate git worktree, I used Antigravity to convert codex blackened with langchain. As expected it did a good job. For langchain I choose gpt & gemini as the API providers. 

The front end looks like below, with the option to select LLM provider and model. 

![][image1]

#### Some design considerations

Entire CV customization logic now implemented with langchain with a RAG component.   
I didn’t use vector databases & LLM embeddings storing and retrieval.   
The main reasons were ;   
(1) the knowledge ( past experience writeups ) base being relatively small &   
(2) Codex’s performance on RAG with simple text search using regex tools with smart keyword search 

As the models get smarter with reasoning and large context lengths, people seem to be focusing on non classic RAG methodologies. I’ve seen commentary and more evidence on this area.   
One such interesting project is [this](http://ca-jobapplier.thankfulocean-b6003de3.eastus.azurecontainerapps.io) where a method to provide structured RAG with keywords, entity search using classic databases. An interesting project to keep an eye on.

After validating my new app works fine locally, I decided to port the app to cloud, using Agent skills

#### Setting up agent to use Azure skills

Antigravity is an agentic IDE and not a pure CLI based agent. However it has a nice ‘Agent Manager’ sub UI that enables you to run multiple agents.

I came across this [Azure plugin for coding agents](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/all-things-azure/announcing-the-azure-skills-plugin/) that packaged both skills & MCPs, claiming to re-architect apps for Azure deployment ( using skills ) and then carry out deployment ( using MCP ). I wanted to try it out with my new standalone app. 

I instructed Antigravity agent to pull the skills and install them, and it did exactly that.  
After authenticating azure cli, I asked Antigravity ; 

```text
I have configured azure cli and authenticated via command line 'az login'. I want a plan to port the current application ( job-applier-agent-langchain ) in this repository to azure. Use azure skill plugin and determine ; 'What Azure services would I need to deploy this project?'
```

It came up with the intended services that I had in mind. ACA, Key Vault. *I wanted to use blob storage instead of File Share, but that is not possible with ACA*  
![][image2]

I want to test the skill and make it bit more complicated, hence asked ; 

```text
instead of using azure container registry I'd like to use git container register. Alter the plan accordingly. I can provid the git access tokens.
```

The agent updated its implementation plan with GHCR.   
*Git Container Registry ( GHCR ) is free to use compared to Azure CR.*

![][image3]

The updated [plan.md](http://plan.md) was ;   
It generated IaaS Code ( bicep ), dockerfile, azure.yaml artefacts for deployment.  
![][image4]

Next, I configured my git with a workflow to build the container using another Antigravity agent. After few attempts and figuring out some dependencies it was successful;

One great thing about Antigravity’s process is that, you can comment on the implementation plan and it revises.

Then, I moved on to creating the Azure resources and instructed Agent to do so;

This is how it deployed resources with bicep.

The agent did a pretty good job and correctly deployed all the resources. My app is now up and running.

![][image6]  
However I’ve missed some details on how to bind the API keys to containers. Got the agent to revise the plan and implement key binding to the container. The revised plan contain setting up RBAC & binding secrets as below;

With that change, I’ve an app version that is deployed on cloud and I can run from anywhere.

My next plan is to extend this app, so that I can give a JD from whatsapp and fine tune the resume via whatsapp. Bit like OpenClaw for my app.

#### Translating to enterprise deployment patterns 

With agent skills, now devops teams can quickly rearchitect any app for cloud deployment.

-The team could maintain a separate skill library that has enterprise vetted deployment templates to comply with standardisation.  
-Have other skills to review IAM policies, bucket policies, trust relationships etc, a governance skill.  
The team's intent and imagination would be the limit here.

However, respecting practical engineering challenges, the teams must spend significant time finetuning such skills.

Most enterprises can obtain Azure or AWS provided OpenAI , Claude endpoints which have more controls in logging and guaranteed content protection. Such endpoints will serve secure coding agents giving more comfort to development & security teams.
